name: Public S3 Bucket Discovered & Drained
description: A backup bucket created by a contractor in 2022 (acme-mktg-archive-old) has been world-readable the whole time. A grayhat researcher finds it via bucket enumeration and starts pulling .sql.gz files. CloudTrail shows AnonymousIdentity GetObject events from a single IP block.
reasoning: Two-tier: a static/marketing S3 'service' (modelled as nginx-style) and the corporate API. The S3 service spikes egress; the API stays calm. The simulation focuses on detection and rotation.

nodes.label: s3-acme-mktg-archive
nodes.notes: World-readable. Holds gzipped DB dumps from 2022.

narrative.text: Quiet baseline. Bucket sees ~5 reads/min from internal jobs.
External IP starts ListObjectsV2 against the bucket — 4000 keys enumerated.
Sequential GetObject for *.sql.gz; egress spikes from 500 KB/s to 80 MB/s.
Bucket policy patched to deny public; credentials rotated for the contractor's old IAM user.
Forensics: 11 GB pulled, including a 2022 customer dump. Breach notification path opened.
Account-wide BlockPublicAccess turned on; SCP to forbid public buckets going forward.
